text_input: Patient is a 62-year-old male admitted with a 20-day history of hiccups and a 3-month history of increased urinary frequency and urgency. Past medical history is significant for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years), Bipolar Affective Disorder, and papillary cystitis. Clinical examination showed stable vitals: BP 130/80 mmHg, Pulse 96 bpm, SpO2 98%, and RR 15 cpm. Laboratory investigations revealed hemoglobin 10.0 g/dL, WBC 6780/µL, platelets 329,000/µL, ESR 91 mm/hr, GRBS 253 mg/dL, and HbA1c 9.5%. Renal and liver function tests were largely normal (Creatinine 0.6 mg/dL, Albumin 3.2 g/dL). Imaging and procedures included an upper GI endoscopy showing LAX LES and antral gastritis, a 2D Echo showing an EF of 58% with mild MR, and a USG showing cystitis and Grade 1 prostatomegaly. The patient was managed with antibiotics (Tufzone, Oflox), insulin (Actrapid, Ryzodeg), and medications for GERD and psychiatric symptoms. The primary diagnosis was hiccups secondary to GERD.
